themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a historical weekly average of 1.0 complaint—a 500% increase (z-score: 7.07)—suggesting either a new enforcement crackdown, vendor proliferation, or quality/safety issues emerging in real-time across Astoria/Long Island City.
evidence: 6 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.07, severity: high)
500% spike indicates either rapid vendor growth or sudden enforcement/quality deterioration
Timing aligns with warm weather season and foot traffic surge in waterfront development zones
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY and DOH about what triggered this week's spike—new vendors, inspections, or resident complaints about hygiene/sidewalk obstruction?
Survey street food vendors in Astoria about recent permitting changes, competition, or enforcement pressure

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Overgrown Branches
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 13 LAST WEEK (395% above 8-week average of 2.6, z-score: 7.37) and overgrown tree/branch complaints hit 10 THIS WEEK (233% above average of 3.0, z-score: 4.67)—together signaling either storm damage, contractor negligence, or deferred maintenance across the district.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 13 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (395% spike, z-score: 7.37)
Overgrown tree/branches: 10 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 4.67)
Combined signal suggests either acute event (storm, contractor work) or chronic DPR maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Check weather logs and DOB permits from past 2 weeks—was there a storm or contractor work triggering tree damage?
Interview DPR about tree maintenance backlog; cross-reference with CB budget requests for DPR capital funding

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Worker/Vehicle Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker or vehicle complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a historical average of 1.2 weekly complaints—a 220% increase (z-score: 6.35)—pointing to potential DSNY service quality, vehicle condition, or driver conduct issues emerging in real-time.
evidence: 4 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (220% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Timing concurrent with warmer weather and increased street activity
Signal suggests acute issue with specific sanitation crew, vehicle maintenance, or resident friction over service
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DSNY for complaints filed against District 401 sanitation operations this week
Interview residents filing complaints—what specific incidents triggered reports (rude staff, overflowing truck, missed pickups)?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle (Uber/Lyft) Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 23 LAST WEEK versus a historical weekly average of 5.2—a 338% increase (z-score: 5.56)—indicating congestion, double-parking, driver conduct, or enforcement activity affecting Astoria/Long Island City's growing gig economy.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.2 weekly average (338% spike, z-score: 5.56)
Likely tied to development surge in Long Island City and increased ride-sharing demand
Overlap with Innovation QNS rezoning completion (EIS final letter sent), suggesting major employment/population activity draw
reporting_angles: Analyze 311 complaint text to identify hotspot streets—are complaints clustered near Innovation QNS, transit hubs, or residential zones?
Interview TLC and NYC DOT about enforcement action or whether they've noticed uptick in congestion complaints from Astoria-LIC

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Concern (Historical)
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints surged to 7 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 weekly average—a 2700% spike (z-score: 10.21)—but has since subsided; this signal is dated and no recent escalation is evident, warranting a follow-up check rather than urgent investigation.
evidence: 7 water quality complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (2700% spike, z-score: 10.21, severity: high)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago and does not appear in recent weekly data—issue may be resolved or cyclical
No current active complaints suggest the issue was acute and temporary (possible main break, discoloration, taste/odor event)
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine root cause of 3-week-old spike and confirm resolution status
Cross-reference with DEP maintenance records and water main break logs for the district from that week
